facts.text: It has been getting steadily worse.
I use insulin for my diabetes.
I gave birth four weeks ago; it was a normal vaginal delivery without complications.
Around the time of the birth I had a vaginal discharge that kept going and wouldn't clear up.
I didn't have a fever with the discharge.

gold.reasoning: 1. Atypical toxoplasmosis was initially considered given the presentation of acute panuveitis — “Patient was admitted with a provisional diagnosis of right acute nongranulomatous panuveitis probably representing atypical toxoplasmosis.” 2. Common infectious and noninfectious causes of uveitis were excluded by laboratory and imaging studies — “a uveitis workup was performed ... which all came to be negative.” 3. Systemic foci of infection, including endocarditis and visceral abscesses, were ruled out — “blood and urine culture; CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis with contrasts; and cardiac echography were performed, which all came to be unremarkable.”

leakage.reason: The vaginal swab result names Candida albicans, the organism of the gold diagnosis; it is the key culture clue, not a statement about the eye.

source_issues: s007 holds two sentences (left eye normal; fluorescein angiography).
No intraocular (vitreous or aqueous) sample result is given; the diagnosis rests on the clinical picture and the vaginal Candida growth.
notes: Index visit: the presentation four weeks postpartum with one week of progressive right-eye vision loss (s001–s008); the uveitis workup (s010–s011) belongs to the same admission, and the later results (s013, s015–s016) are given a time.
s014 (persistent peripartum vaginal discharge without fever) was elicited later but is the patient's own history, so it gives facts f007 and f008.
The eye findings (keratic precipitates, vitreous haze, retinal infiltrates) need a slit lamp or fundoscopy, so they are findings only; the patient-noticeable symptom is the vision loss.

excluded_sentences.reason: Admission with a provisional diagnosis (acute nongranulomatous panuveitis, probably atypical toxoplasmosis): clinician reasoning, not a finding.
Empirical treatment (clindamycin, co-trimoxazole, prednisolone) and its response: treatment during the workup.
